counties.adjudication_rationale: The selected project's 2017 page-history anchor is too late for county treatment. Storey County publicly welcomed Switch's planned $1 billion, three-million-square-foot campus on January 16, 2015, Nevada approved the Storey data-center abatement in July, and contemporaneous reporting documented active grading by September 15. The county fire department subsequently reported that the pad was at grade and concrete was being poured continuously during 2015. No reviewed record establishes an earlier E3-scale data center in Storey County, but historical enterprise, telecom and permit inventories remain incomplete. September 15, 2015 is therefore a provisional physical-construction upper bound, not a causal-ready first-exposure date; concurrent Tesla Gigafactory construction is a separate severe contamination risk for any county-outcome design.

counties.adjudication_rationale: Meta Eagle Mountain is not Utah County's first economically material data-center exposure. The NSA awarded a multi-million-dollar Utah Data Center utility-infrastructure contract on May 28, 2010 for power, water, sewer and storm drainage at Camp Williams. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers then broke ground on January 6, 2011 on a $1.2 billion, one-million-square-foot campus expected to create 5,000-10,000 construction jobs and 100-200 permanent jobs. Utah environmental records explicitly place the operating facility in Utah County and document 62 standby generators. These facts satisfy multiple E3 materiality indicators and reject Meta's 2018/2021 chronology as a county first-entry anchor. Fibernet's 2002 Orem colocation facility, a hosted Lindon center, C7's 2007 Lindon facility and the incomplete institutional and enterprise inventory leave the true first E3 date unresolved, so May 28, 2010 is retained only as a documented upper bound.
